title: Metric creep in standard.py and types.py
final_text:
Work complete.

**What I found.** Auditing the bytes actually in this sandbox against the no-metric rule:

- **Nothing forbidden (no F rows).** No count, rate, rank, average, majority or "best" in `standard.py` or `types.py` reaches adjudication or a reading's standing. The guard parameters, word limits, replicate floor, panel shape, budgets and wall clocks are all allowed instrument/spend bounds (A rows). The ceiling's "printed with counts" block register carries its own denial of warrant in the same clause.
- **Three live C rows:**
  1. `types.py AuditConfig.judge_err_max` / `streak_max` — a rate and a streak count whose only consumer would be the absent AUDIT/DECIDE wave; probe showed they occur only in `types.py` and decide nothing as shipped, but the per-seat prohibition is prose-only.
  2. `standard.py assert_config_matches_standard` / `types.py SeatsConfig` — dual owners of the panel-shape numbers; the docstring-mandated PREFLIGHT (W5) reconciliation call has no caller in this sandbox, and a probe showed a contradicting `SeatsConfig` loads without refusal.
  3. The wave-0 oracle itself: `HouseRules.test_every_integer_in_the_body_is_a_declared_guard_parameter` FAILS on the shipped body (four integers under `role_contracts.word_limits.*` that the module docstring documents but the oracle was never updated to admit) — a permanently red oracle is the creep vector the task names. Not F in the code (the integers are allowed bounds), C on the oracle.

**Files written:** `out/metric-creep.md` (the table and verdicts), and probes `probe/probe_audit_thresholds.py`, `probe/probe_integer_oracle.py`, `probe/probe_preflight_reconciliation.py` — each run with `python3 probe/<name>.py`, all exit 0.

**Last test run:** `python3 run_tests.py docs.examples.test_standard_example` — exit code 1: 4 subtests FAIL (the oracle drift on `role_contracts.word_limits.*`, confirming row 10 against the shipped bytes), 3 ERRORs caused by sandbox-absent C001 PLAN.md/material.json data files (not drift), all other tests pass. No source modules were modified.
